retention.what: photographic evidence if no notice of speeding violation is issued
retention.period: up to five days

retention.what: confidential DMV information used to issue notices of violation
retention.period: up to 120 days after final disposition of notice of speeding violation

name: Red Light and No-Turn Enforcement cameras
purpose: Cite and prosecute red-light and illegal-turn violations, and use the data for engineering analysis such as vehicle counts, speeds and violation numbers.
collects: three digital photos per event: two of the rear and one of the front of the violating vehicle (front photo captures the driver)
short HD video clip of the violation
violation data stamped on each image (date/time/lane/red-light time)
3D radar tracking of vehicle position, speed and direction
registered owner's name, address and identifying information from the California DMV or another state/country's agency
continuous intersection video on the camera, overwritten every 30 days
identifies_people: Yes. Photographs the license plate and the driver's face (citation includes a close-up of the driver), and DMV supplies the registered owner's name and address. Passengers captured in violation photos are blurred.

retention.what: events that do not result in a citation (driver information, data, images)
retention.period: Contractor must destroy within 15 Business Days of determining the Event does not meet the City's Business Rules, or SFPD's rejection of the Event

retention.what: violations that result in a citation (all related information incl. data, images, paper records)
retention.period: Contractor must destroy within 15 Business Days of final disposition; if notice of final disposition is not received from the Superior Court, within 5 years of the Citation due date

retention.what: continuous video recorded on cameras at the intersection
retention.period: overwritten every 30 days; only brief clips of potential violations are uploaded to the Contractor

retention.what: any PII data, exception
retention.period: may be kept beyond the standard period for litigation holds, court orders, search warrants, subpoenas

shared_internal: Superior Court (daily XML/PDF reports with violation photos, citation info and driver details incl. name, address, date of birth, height, weight; policy lists the court as internal)
shared_external: Verra Mobility (the Contractor: owns, operates and maintains the system, reviews violations, processes, prints and mails citations; contract signed Aug 21, 2018)
outside_law_enforcement_access: Photographic records are confidential under Vehicle Code 21455.5(f) and available 'only to governmental agencies and law enforcement agencies'. Policy says 'a search warrant or subpoena signed by a judge is required to share PII data' outside the normal process. Out-of-state and federal agencies are not specifically addressed.
audit: No access-log or audit-log requirement stated. Compliance is enforced through the Verra Mobility contract (insurance, encryption, liquidated damages for loss of violation data). Contractor performs monthly quality-control audits of rejected events. Oversight: Automated Enforcement Program Manager (1824 Principal Administrative Analyst).

name: Security Cameras (fixed and mobile: facilities, stations, garages, signal poles, transit vehicles)
purpose: Live monitoring and recording of video to protect staff, patrons and facilities, review incidents, give footage to law enforcement, enforce parking and driving violations, and train transit operators from on-board video.

date and time
geolocation data (TXT, CSV, DOCX)

name: Driver-Safety Video Analytics (DriveCam event recorders on buses)
purpose: Record g-force-triggered video and audio events on buses to analyze collisions, passenger falls, driver training issues and misconduct, infrastructure problems and customer complaints.
collects: 12 seconds of video AND audio per event (8 seconds before and 4 seconds after a g-force trigger)
event reports (HTML, downloaded as PDF)
event data such as location, date/time, bus speed, trigger type and g-forces
AI-flagged driver behaviors (e.g., talking on cell phone, eating while driving, drowsy/sleeping, speeding, rolling stops)
identifies_people: Used to identify driver training issues, misconduct or negligence; follow-up actions include training and discipline, and videos/reports are treated as confidential personnel records. Policy says it is not used to monitor passengers or the public.

retention.what: video and PDF reports (by Department)
retention.period: retained 365 days by vendor, then deleted on day 366

retention.what: video uploaded to the Lytx data center
retention.period: retained and available for 90 days, then stored on backup media for an additional 275 days; deleted from data center on 91st day and from backup media on 276th day

retention.what: video that warrants further investigation
retention.period: Department may retain longer on its servers (no limit stated)

name: SFPD Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR)
purpose: Locate stolen or wanted vehicles, wanted persons, victims and missing people, support criminal investigations and counter-terrorism by reading license plates against hotlists.
collects: digital images of vehicle license plates and their associated vehicles
date and time the plate passed an ALPR site
geo-location (named in the use rules; amended policy lists time and geo-location metadata)
video and still images in common formats (added in amended policy)
identifies_people: Policy states 'ALPR does not collect PII' (both documents) and the amended policy says an ALPR alert will not on its own identify an individual. However, authorized uses include locating wanted persons, suspects and victims by plate.

retention.what: ALPR records (SFPD defers to the NCRIC retention standard)
retention.period: 12 months from capture

retention.what: records connected to a criminal investigation or criminal intelligence file
retention.period: may be retained for 5 years

retention.what: data downloaded, copied or printed for a criminal investigation
retention.period: kept through adjudication of a case, an appeals process and statute of limitations (no number stated)

shared_internal: Public Defender's Office or criminal defense attorney, via the District Attorney's Office under California discovery laws
SFPD personnel: sworn members, civilian crime analysts; radio shop technicians (hardware only)
shared_external: NCRIC (Northern California Regional Intelligence Center) hosts the data repositories; amended policy adds 'and/or any other vendor utilized by the Department'
NCRIC law enforcement partners, for a criminal or administrative investigation
Parties to civil litigation or other third parties, in response to a valid Court Order

AMENDED policy adds (citing Civil Code 1798.90.55): SFPD shall not sell, share or transfer ALPR information except to another public agency as permitted by state law, and not to out-of-state or federal agencies 'without a court order or warrant issued by a California court'; hosting and towing services do not count as sharing. Amended Appendix A also says NCRIC-hosted data is not used for enforcement of immigration laws.

Access via BOSS (Back Office Server Software) or other vendor applications; users need approval, access must be tied to an investigation or authorized use; CLETS and DGO 10.08 apply. Oversight: Deputy Chief of Investigations and Lieutenant of Special Investigations Division; violations go to Internal Affairs. Amended policy says the Department will 'evaluate the impact of the technology on the following measures' annually, but the list is blank in the text.
